def: A belief a project plan depends on that nobody has yet checked, such as that the data may be sent to a hosted model or that users will adopt the tool.
An assumption that, if false, makes the whole plan pointless however well the rest is built; Eric Ries's term in The Lean Startup.

term: Expected weeks saved per day of testing
def: A ranking score for assumptions: the chance an assumption is false times the weeks wasted if it fails late, divided by the days a small test would take.
An assumption written with the evidence, the amount and the consequence named, so that some observation could contradict it.
Adjusting a prompt or system after seeing failures on the test cases until the score rises, so the final score describes the tuning effort and not the system's quality on new cases.
A scripted experiment with real cases in a file, one fixed prompt and a scorer that compares outputs to labels the expert wrote first.
A prototype that looks like a finished system to its users while a person behind the scenes produces the outputs, used to learn about behaviour before automating.
An open version of manual delivery in which the customer knows a person is doing the work by hand, so the builder learns which parts of the job matter.
